extracted.intended_audience: aspiring short-story writers and beginning-to-intermediate fiction authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting, revising, and submitting short stories (1,000–10,000 words), emphasizing a single central premise, tight cast, strong opening, and iterative editing. Targets writers preparing complete short fiction for publication or contests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick a simple, central premise
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief, powerful concept (e.g., Kafka's man-becomes-insect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one clear conceit or central idea that drives the story; keep it focused so every scene and detail supports that core premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a small but distinct cast of characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a limited number of characters who are distinguishable through appearance, behavior, speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the cast to avoid clutter; make each character recognizable via specific physical traits, recurring behaviors, and distinct voice so readers can track them easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin writing close to the end
rubrics_metrics.description: Start in media res near the climax; avoid preliminary exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the story near the pivotal moment to maintain narrative momentum and reader interest; defer backstory and expansive setup until after the scene or weave it in sparingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shut out your internal editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Write freely in the first draft—'anything goes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During drafting, silence the inner critic to keep momentum; allow imperfect prose and bad ideas, knowing you'll refine them in revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish the first draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the draft; endings are crucial—avoid being too obvious or confusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to finishing the story to discover its shape; craft an ending that feels earned and resonant without telegraphing every outcome or leaving readers bewildered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit the short story
rubrics_metrics.description: Tighten threads and eliminate unnecessary elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise for clarity, pacing, and economy: remove scenes, lines, or characters that don't serve the central premise; sharpen language and ensure thematic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share with beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit feedback after stepping away for weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the manuscript rest before asking for critique; pick readers who can comment on clarity, emotional impact, pacing, and whether the premise and ending land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit to publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit to traditional publishers, contests, or self-publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research markets and their guidelines, tailor submissions to target venues, follow formatting and simultaneous-submission rules, and choose the path (submission/contest/self-pub) that fits your goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for this range depending on the market and story type (flash at the low end, standard short story toward the middle/high end); adjust to fit the story's needs and publication targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Character, conflict, plot structure, POV, setting, theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure these elements are present and integrated: characters must drive conflict, plot structure should build to a meaningful moment, POV must be consistent, setting should support mood, and theme should emerge from action rather than exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentence must "pique the reader's curiosity, raises questions, and keeps them reading."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft an opening that immediately engages—use a striking image, surprising fact, provocative line, or immediate action to create questions and momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Philosophy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat revision as essential; expect multiple passes to refine structure, language, and thematic clarity rather than relying on the first draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story scope and mood
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories typically encapsulate a mood, covering minimal incidents with a limited cast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a single mood, effect, or turning point; limit the number of incidents and characters to maintain intensity, unity, and emotional resonance.
